notes: Authored fields: domain, cluster, kind, role, maturity, verified_on, triggers, related, evidence_refs, trigger_family (effect cards only), surfaces (effect cards only). Generated fields (description, body_lines, scripts, evidence_count) are overwritten by 'python tools/skillkit.py index --write'.

skills.name: grep-cannot-read-a-compressed-store
triggers: recover userscripts after a profile move
skills.description: Use when you need a userscript's real source, its stored settings, or to recover scripts after a profile move — and "grep finds nothing", "strings shows garbage", or the file looks empty. The idea: browser extension stores are Snappy-compressed LevelDB with double-encoded JSON values, so text tools cannot see anything; the data is there, it just needs a decoder rather than a search.

skills.name: measure-the-rendering-path
skills.description: Use when choosing how to draw something — sprite atlas vs per-item text, canvas vs DOM, WebGL vs CSS — or when a canvas is slow and the plan is to "optimize it later". The idea: the rendering path is a measured decision, and the widely repeated advice is not always right (a pre-rendered atlas lost to plain fillText by 7.5x here); three lines of benchmark beat a day of architecture.

skills.name: mvcreate
skills.description: Use when a song, a mood or a script has to become a short, phone-first video drawn entirely in code — pixel art, CRT, hand-drawn picture book or low-poly 3D — and it must read as deliberate rather than generated. Symptoms: "make an MV shot", "the style is right but the character is mush on a phone", "it looks cheap / not really pixel / not really 3D", "every render comes out different", "the loop jumps at the seam".

skills.name: one-press-one-action
skills.description: Use when a single click or tap produces two effects — "the toggle undoes itself", "click fires twice", "it collapses and instantly restores" — or when a gesture handler is shared by several pointer events. The idea: one physical press emits several events (pointerup plus lostpointercapture, sometimes pointercancel), so routing them all to one handler without a state guard makes every press act twice.

skills.name: precompute-the-rest-state
triggers: physics toy never comes to rest
skills.description: Use when a system has to end in a canonical configuration after the user damages it — physics piles, layout animations, undo/restore, drag toys — and instead it "never settles", "jitters forever", "particles shuffle after landing", "the restore bounces", or a state machine is stuck in `collapsing`. The idea: compute the end state and animate toward it; never simulate your way into it.

skills.name: render-it-or-you-are-guessing
skills.description: Use when a page must be understood but cannot be read — JS-only SPAs, "can you see this site?", consent or interstitial gates that need a click, screenshots that must be compared across viewports, or a change that has to be verified visually. The idea: the DOM you can fetch is not the page the user sees, and the cheap tools lie in three specific ways — static fetch returns an empty shell, DOM dumping cannot click, and a screenshot taken on load fires before the page is ready.

skills.name: the-entry-bundle-lies
triggers: is this WebGL or an image
what is this site built with
what interaction techniques does this site use
the lazy chunk holds the renderer
skills.description: Use when asked what a site is built with, why a page is heavy, or which interaction techniques it uses — before optimising, rewriting or copying it. The idea: the entry bundle is the least informative file in the project, because the interesting code is code-split into lazy chunks; an audit that stops at the entry file produces confidently wrong answers, and an extraction is finished only when someone could implement each finding.

skills.name: the-halo-remembers-the-cursor
triggers: cursor glow looks like a flashlight
the halo feels glued to the pointer
want an ink or smoke trail behind the cursor
page feels dead until the mouse moves
skills.description: Use when a cursor effect feels dead or glued — a glow that sits on the pointer like a flashlight, a page that only wakes when you move — and you want an ink halo that blooms behind the cursor, keeps the shape of the path for a moment, then fades on its own. The idea: the halo is a velocity field with memory, not a sprite that follows the pointer.

skills.name: the-probe-lies
triggers: ENOENT for a file that exists
the check passed but it is still broken
skills.description: Use when a check comes back negative but the symptom persists — "no dump found", "grep finds nothing", "the config says otherwise", "ENOENT for a file that exists", "the test passed but it is still broken" — and you are about to conclude the thing is not there. The idea: a negative probe is evidence about the probe, not about the world; find the probe that can be positive.

skills.name: the-shell-is-what-ships
triggers: the shader is done but the page is not
skills.description: Use when building or reviewing an immersive hero, shader scene or full-bleed canvas — "the shader is done but the page is not", WebGL hero fallback, context loss, a loading state that never resolves, or a showcase that renders beautifully on the author's machine. The idea: the renderer is the demo and the shell is the product — state machine, fallback, frame-loop hygiene, input parity and responsive framing are what decide whether it ships.
